deals.proximityHighways: Just off Interstate 95 (59,500 AADT) — one of the East Coast's most active freight and travel corridors — with direct access from W 5th Street (14,000 AADT). Lumberton Regional Airport is nearby.
deals.retailCotenants: Lumberton Towne Center and Biggs Park Mall (currently undergoing major renovations and adding new retailers) are the competing retail concentrations in the trade area.

tenants.name: Dollar Tree
tenants.creditRating: Investment grade (Dollar Tree, Inc. — BBB category)
tenants.assumptionNote: EXPIRES 31 DECEMBER 2027 — the first roll in the hold, on 12% of GLA, and the center's strongest credit. Healthy at $157 PSF of sales and a 5.62% health ratio (OM-stated), and at $6.74/SF the rent is deeply below CBRE's $7.00-$15.00/SF large-shop market range, so renewal economics should favor the landlord. CBRE excludes Dollar Tree from the general vacancy-loss factor. 18 years of tenure.

tenants.name: China Garden
tenants.assumptionNote: WORST TENANT HEALTH AT THE CENTER — $138 PSF of sales against a 16.59% health ratio (OM-stated), roughly double a comfortable restaurant occupancy cost. At $19.84/SF this is the second-highest rent in the center and the sales do not support it. The lease runs to December 2030, so this is a mid-hold credit and renewal risk rather than a near-term one, but it is the row most likely to go dark.

tenants.name: Rent-A-Center
tenants.assumptionNote: 34 years of tenure — in place since August 1992. CBRE excludes it from the general vacancy-loss factor. Rent-to-own is a category with above-average credit and regulatory sensitivity. No sales disclosed.

tenants.name: Pizza Hut
tenants.parentCompany: Yum! Brands, Inc. (franchised location — franchisee not disclosed)
tenants.assumptionNote: Franchised QSR — confirm the contracting entity and any guaranty. Pizza Hut's US dine-in footprint has been shrinking; a franchisee-level bankruptcy is the risk to watch. No sales disclosed.

tenants.name: Top Nail
tenants.assumptionNote: Highest rent PSF at the center ($20.70) and the second-longest term (November 2033). 17 years of tenure. No sales disclosed — at this rent level that matters.

tenants.name: Missy's Beauty
tenants.reimbursementMethod: GROSS or fully-abated recovery — the OM models ZERO expense reimbursement in CY2027 on 9,100 SF. Ownership absorbs CAM, taxes and insurance on 13.6% of the GLA. Confirm the structure against the lease.
tenants.assumptionNote: SECOND-LARGEST SUITE (13.6% of GLA) at the LOWEST rent in the center, $4.22/SF, and with NO expense recovery at all — the two facts compound. A beauty-supply operator on 9,100 SF at $4.22/SF gross is well below CBRE's $7.00-$15.00 large-shop market range even before adding back the ~$2.50/SF of expenses ownership absorbs. Real mark-to-market on renewal in October 2029, but no sales are disclosed to judge whether the tenant could pay more.

tenants.name: Food Lion
tenants.reimbursementMethod: NNN. Recovery of only $1.03/SF is far below the center's $2.50-$3.00/SF shop rate — a capped or subsidized grocery structure. Confirm against the lease.
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $5.13/SF ($155,250) in CY2027 through the June 2032 expiry.
tenants.assumptionNote: THE ANCHOR: 45.3% of GLA, 29% of base rent, 29% of total revenue, in place since August 1985 (41 years). An excellent store — $393 PSF of sales at a 1.57% health ratio (OM-stated), which back-solves to roughly $11.9 million of annual sales. NOTE A CONFLICT IN THE OM: page 3 states 'consistent sales of ~$11.3M', but the rent roll's own $393 PSF on 30,280 SF and the printed 1.57% health ratio both imply ~$11.9M. The $393 PSF and 1.57% are recorded here because they are internally consistent with the rent roll; confirm the dollar figure. At $5.13/SF the rent is far below market, which makes this secure, extremely sticky income rather than capturable upside. Recovery is only $1.03/SF — a capped grocery structure that leaves ownership carrying expense growth on 45% of the GLA. CBRE excludes Food Lion from the general vacancy-loss factor. The OM does not disclose renewal options — get them from the lease.

tenants.name: Pawn Plus
tenants.rentBumps: Site plan prints a current rate of $11.13/SF; the CY2027 pro-forma blends to $12.10/SF, implying a contractual step during 2027.
tenants.rentSchedule: Current $11.13/SF stepping to a CY2027 average of $12.10/SF ($75,046). Individual steps not printed.
tenants.assumptionNote: Third-largest suite (9.3% of GLA) and the second-largest base rent after Food Lion. Pawn is a use category with regulatory sensitivity and can complicate financing and future re-tenanting — confirm any use restrictions. No sales disclosed.

tenants.name: Subway
tenants.parentCompany: Subway (Roark Capital) — franchised location; franchisee not disclosed
tenants.assumptionNote: Franchised QSR — confirm the contracting entity and any guaranty. No sales disclosed.

tenants.parentCompany: Jackson Hewitt Tax Service Inc. (franchised location — franchisee not disclosed)
tenants.assumptionNote: HIGHEST RENT PSF AT THE CENTER at $25.20/SF — 24% above the next-highest shop and roughly 3x the center average — for a SEASONAL tax-preparation use that generates revenue mainly from January to April. No sales are disclosed. This is the row where an above-market rent is most likely to reset down at the December 2029 expiry; do not treat it as a comp for the rest of the center.

tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $11.66/SF ($27,984) in CY2027 through the August 2028 expiry.
tenants.assumptionNote: Tobacco retail — a regulatory- and headline-risk use category. Expires August 2028. No sales disclosed.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $463,149 in-place NOI, the $101,714 recovery line and the $641,617 effective gross revenue tie to. This OM prints FULL lease dates (MM/DD/YY) on the pro-forma, so no date convention was needed.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) roster SF sums to 66,781 = the stated GLA, with no vacancy (100% occupied); (b) base rents sum to $539,904 vs the $539,903 printed (rounding); (c) tenant recoveries sum to $101,715 vs the $101,714 printed (rounding); (d) $641,617 EGR - $178,468 OpEx = $463,149 NOI.

WALT of 4.04 years is the OM-stated figure and reproduces to 4.03 when computed SF-weighted from the roster's expiries as of 01/01/2027 (the analysis commencement date) — an independent confirmation the roster is complete.

TWO HEADLINE FIGURES DIFFER: page 9's in-place EGR is $641,617 with NO general vacancy loss (giving the $463,149 headline NOI), while page 10's CY2027 cash flow applies a $6,365 general vacancy loss, giving $635,252 of EGR and $456,785 of NOI. The $463,149 in-place figure is recorded as the deal NOI, and the CY2027 cash-flow row carries the $456,785. The 1.4% difference is the vacancy-loss factor, not an error.

FOOD LION SALES CONFLICT INSIDE THE OM: page 3 says 'consistent sales of ~$11.3M', but the rent roll's $393 PSF on 30,280 SF implies ~$11.9M, and the printed 1.57% health ratio back-solves to ~$11.87M. The $393 PSF and 1.57% are recorded because they are internally consistent with the rent roll's own base rent and recoveries; treat the $11.3M as the outlier and confirm with the seller.

THE DEMOGRAPHICS PAGE'S HOUSEHOLDS BLOCK IS INTERNALLY BROKEN and should not be used. It reports 1,795 households within 1 mile against a 1-mile population of 474 and only 233 occupied housing units, and 23,216 households within 3 miles against a 3-mile population of 12,227 — more households than people. The Population, Household Income and Housing Units blocks are internally coherent and are what has been captured here (population3mi 12,227; avgHHIncome3mi $60,253; medianHHIncome3mi $49,095). Ask CBRE to re-run the households figures.

TWO TENANTS RECOVER LITTLE OR NOTHING: Missy's Beauty ($0 on 9,100 SF, 13.6% of GLA) and Food Lion ($1.03/SF on 30,280 SF, 45.3% of GLA, against a $2.50-$3.00/SF shop rate). Together that is 59% of the GLA on capped, subsidized or gross structures, which is why the center recovers only $101,714 against $178,468 of operating expenses — a 57% recovery ratio that is weak for a center presented as NNN. Verify both structures against the leases.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $463,149 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. The $49,558 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. Robeson County, NC reassesses on a multi-year cycle rather than on sale, so the step-up risk here is more about the next county-wide revaluation than about the transaction itself — but confirm the county's cycle year.

Expenses are CBRE's model of the 2026 Budget GROWN 3% (this book differs from the others in the portfolio, which use the budget unadjusted), with non-recoverable ownership-specific expenses replaced by a $0.05/SF assumption.
The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: THE TRADE AREA IS SHRINKING. 3-mile population fell from 15,910 in 2010 to 12,794 in 2020 to 12,227 in 2025 — down 23% in fifteen years — and is projected to decline a further 0.22% over the next five years. 5-mile population is down from 33,802 to 28,410 over the same period. Three-mile average household income is $60,253 with a median of $49,095. A declining, low-income trade area is the single most important fact about this asset and it argues for real cap-rate cushion and conservative rent-growth assumptions, whatever the mark-to-market spread looks like on paper.

Dollar Tree — the center's best credit and 12% of GLA — expires 31 December 2027, in the first year of the hold, with no disclosed renewal option. CBRE's in-place NOI assumes it holds over at current terms with no downtime or re-leasing cost.

59% OF THE GLA RECOVERS LITTLE OR NOTHING. Missy's Beauty (9,100 SF) recovers $0 and Food Lion (30,280 SF) recovers only $1.03/SF against the center's $2.50-$3.00/SF shop rate. The center recovers $101,714 against $178,468 of operating expenses — a 57% recovery ratio. Every dollar of expense growth on those two suites, including the next Robeson County revaluation, falls to ownership.

China Garden carries a 16.59% occupancy cost on $138 PSF of sales (OM-stated) at the center's second-highest rent, $19.84/SF. That ratio is roughly double a sustainable restaurant level. The lease runs to December 2030 but this is the row most likely to go dark.

Jackson Hewitt pays $25.20/SF — the highest rent at the center, roughly 3x the center average — for a SEASONAL tax-preparation use with no disclosed sales. That is above-market rent that may not survive the December 2029 renewal, and it inflates the in-place NOI a buyer would capitalize. Do not read it as a market comp.

The OM's own page-3 sales figure for Food Lion (~$11.3M) does not reconcile with the rent roll's $393 PSF and 1.57% health ratio, both of which imply ~$11.9M. A 5% discrepancy on the anchor's sales in a four-bullet highlights page is worth running down.

Sales are disclosed for only three of eleven tenants (Food Lion, Dollar Tree, China Garden), and one of the three is the center's problem tenant. Nothing is known about Missy's Beauty, Pawn Plus, Rent-A-Center or Jackson Hewitt — 21,900 SF and 35% of base rent between them.
Two of eleven suites are tobacco/vape or pawn uses (Express Discount Tobacco, Pawn Plus) — categories that carry regulatory sensitivity and can complicate financing and future re-tenanting.
Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma, and with 59% of the GLA on capped or gross recovery structures, a revaluation flows disproportionately to ownership.

upsideItems.item: 24,900 SF of renewals inside the hold
upsideItems.detail: 24,900 SF rolls between 2029 and 2031 (Pizza Hut, Missy's Beauty, Subway, Jackson Hewitt, China Garden, Pawn Plus and Rent-A-Center), which is the OM's stated mark-to-market window. In-place rent is $8.08/SF against CBRE's $10.32/SF 2027 weighted-average market rent, and the modeled cash flow takes NOI from $456,785 in CY2027 to $617,227 by CY2032 largely on those renewals.

upsideItems.item: Recast Missy's Beauty from gross to market NNN
upsideItems.detail: Missy's Beauty is the deepest single opportunity: 9,100 SF (13.6% of GLA) at $4.22/SF on a gross structure, against a $7.00-$15.00/SF large-shop market range. Recasting it to NNN at market would move both the rent and the recovery ratio. It expires October 2029.

upsideItems.item: Food Lion is secure, deeply below-market income
upsideItems.detail: Food Lion at $5.13/SF on 45.3% of GLA is far below market and, with a 1.57% occupancy cost on ~$11.9M of sales, is exceptionally secure income. The store has operated here since 1985. Treat it as durability rather than capturable upside — the June 2032 expiry sits at the edge of a normal hold and the OM discloses no option structure.

upsideItems.item: Dollar Tree renewal at a 5.62% occupancy cost
upsideItems.detail: Dollar Tree at $6.74/SF with a 5.62% occupancy cost has clear room on renewal, and its December 2027 expiry brings that conversation forward into year one.

upsideItems.item: 100% leased — no lease-up risk or vacancy carry
upsideItems.detail: 100% occupied with no lease-up risk and no vacancy carry — unusual in this portfolio group, and it means the growth comes from renewals rather than from speculative absorption.

Exceptional interstate exposure: immediately off I-95 at 59,500 AADT, one of the East Coast's busiest freight and travel corridors, with W 5th Street frontage at 14,000 AADT. That traffic supports the QSR and convenience tenancy independent of the resident base.

upsideItems.item: Biggs Park Mall renovation lifts the node
upsideItems.detail: Biggs Park Mall in the trade area is undergoing major renovations and adding retailers, which should help the broader node.

deals.notes: Lumber River is a 66,781 SF Food Lion-anchored neighborhood center immediately off Interstate 95 (59,500 AADT) on W 5th Street in Lumberton, North Carolina, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 100% leased — the only fully-occupied asset in this group other than Fort Howard Square — and produces $463,149 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $641,617 of effective gross revenue against $178,468 of operating expenses, at an $8.08/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $10.32/SF modeled market rent. Food Lion has anchored the center since August 1985, occupies 45.3% of the GLA at $5.13/SF, and runs an excellent store at roughly $11.9 million of sales, $393 PSF, and a 1.57% occupancy cost; the co-tenancy is genuinely national for a market this size, with Dollar Tree, Rent-A-Center, Pizza Hut and Subway. The value-add case is the 24,900 SF rolling between 2029 and 2031 plus two deeply below-market suites — Missy's Beauty at $4.22/SF gross on 9,100 SF and Dollar Tree at $6.74/SF against a 5.62% occupancy cost. Two things cut against it. First, the trade area is contracting: 3-mile population has fallen 23% since 2010, to 12,227, with a $49,095 median household income and a further decline projected — mark-to-market spreads mean less where the customer base is shrinking, and this deserves genuine cap-rate cushion. Second, 59% of the GLA recovers little or nothing, because Missy's Beauty pays gross and Food Lion recovers only $1.03/SF, leaving a 57% expense-recovery ratio and putting the next Robeson County revaluation squarely on ownership. Watch China Garden, which carries a 16.59% occupancy cost at the center's second-highest rent, and Jackson Hewitt, whose $25.20/SF on a seasonal use is above-market rent inflating the in-place NOI rather than a comp to build on.
